title: nucleus -- the cell's ledger record envelope and the 19-kind taxonomy
$comment: Generated mirror of contracts/nucleus.md v5.1.0 (P3 resolution) -- the .md is the source of truth; regenerate on any bump (CONTRACT-HDR-1).
description: Root = one ledger record (nucleus.md sec 2: JSONL, one per line, UTF-8, append-only). The 19 kind bodies (sec 3 taxonomy, 4 families, closed) are $defs keyed by kind name. Reader liberality (G4): emitters write exactly the envelope shape; readers MUST ignore unknown fields and unknown kinds (folds return state unchanged), never error, and preserve unknown fields on re-serialize. Kind bodies are modeled from the sec 3 'body essentials' column and are therefore open (additionalProperties true).

seq.$comment: 1-based, dense, monotonic. THE order. Never order by ts (sec 2)

kind.$comment: sec 3 taxonomy -- 19 kinds, 4 families (io/control/memory/structure), closed at emit; unknown kinds ignored by folds at read. Removed v0.1 kinds: handoff, system

refs.$comment: prior seqs this record depends on (strictly < seq; only the past is citable -- sec 6.1 rule 2)

red.$comment: OPTIONAL redaction note, ANY kind -- the membrane redacted body content pre-append; absence is auditable (identity-firewall.md owns the rule set)

body.$comment: kind-specific (sec 3; $defs below). A body > 8 KB or binary becomes an artifact spill {artifact: {rel, sha256, bytes, mime}} (sec 2; $defs/artifact_spill)

prev.$comment: previous record's hash (hex). Anchors: root cells prev0 = sha256('hypercell/nucleus-chain/1' 0x00 claim_id); forked children prev0 = parent.hash(at_seq). Chain constant versioned independently of this contract

hash.$comment: chain column -- construction is wire.md sec 5.1's, the ONE home (canon #11: leaf = sha256(canon(record sans hash/sig)); hash_n = sha256(raw32(prev) concat raw32(leaf))); this contract CITES it and never restates it. canon = RFC-8785 JCS (common/canon.py, shared with the Medium chain)

artifact_spill.$comment: sec 2 artifact spill -- the record hash covers the artifact's sha256, so tamper-evidence extends to spilled bytes

census.$comment: genesis contract census (sec 1): ALWAYS the FULL 9-TUPLE -- all nine contract axes at EVERY depth that has a ledger at all (d0 has none; s2-34). A partial census is refused at spawn, never defaulted. In-chain => tamper-evident => foldable

percept.$comment: io family (sec 3). Trust tags are stamped by the membrane at ingress, before append -- the firewall contract owns stamping rules; this contract owns propagation. A record whose trust tag is absent reads as external (fail-closed). R13 legacy mapping applies to PRE-ADOPTION records only (seq < chain_adopted_at_seq, resting on the s6-12 signed baseline): source operator -> trust operator, every other legacy percept -> external; post-adoption absent -> external, no source fallback, ever (sec 14 rule 2)

reason.$comment: source=wake: waking is perceiving -- percept{source: wake, body:{reason, waited_ms, filter}} (sec 3)

decision.$comment: io family (sec 3) -- model-authored choice (d2+, OPTIONAL); DECISION-CLASS for the register wall (sec 6.1)

action.$comment: io family (sec 3) -- gold if H1+ (LAW-FSYNC-EFFECT, sec 4); args ride inline ('{verb, args...}')

outcome.$comment: io family (sec 3) -- gold iff its action was gold; the read-barrier's stored answer (outcome_for(idem))

cost.$comment: nucleus-local cost shape: integer micro-USD and integer ms (sec 2 canon note -- floats are cross-language canon hazards); distinct from the Medium cost{} field-group

genesis.$comment: control family; seq 1, exactly once, gold (sec 1). A spawn against a claim-id with prior Medium receipts but no genesis (or failing chain verify) MUST be REFUSED

lineage_root.$comment: own claim if root; inherited if forked

anyOf.$comment: the borrowed-segment manifest (sec 10 step 4): LOGICAL prefix; hardlink is a same-filesystem fast path only

chain_adopted_at_seq.$comment: synthetic genesis (HONEST-EPOCH, sec 1): records < k are immutable-but-unhashed and the contract says so

pre_adoption_root.$comment: s6-12 (MUST at migration): RFC-6962 Merkle root over the pre-adoption records (seq < chain_adopted_at_seq, canon bytes), bound into the OPERATOR-SIGNED synthetic genesis -- post-migration tampering of the unhashed region is detectable against a signed baseline; the R13 legacy trust-tag read and the signed export (identity-firewall.md B.7) rest on it

checkpoint.$comment: control family (sec 3) -- gold when ack-bearing (LAW-FSYNC-ACK); a cell's Medium cursor advances ONLY inside a checkpoint (LAW-CURSOR-IN-CHECKPOINT, sec 4)

nucleus.stats.$comment: control family (sec 3/12) -- written by the nucleus itself, one per checkpoint or per 512 appends; feeds NUC-7 tier bars

parked.$comment: control family (sec 3/10) -- gold; metadata, NEVER load-bearing for resume (a crash-park writes nothing and resume works identically)

repair.$comment: control family (sec 3/8) -- gold; written by the nucleus on open after a torn tail moves to ledger.torn-<ts>

contract_bump.$comment: control family (sec 1/3) -- gold; a version transition appended INSIDE the chain (outside it a version epoch can be retro-claimed)

memory.assert.$comment: memory family (sec 3/6) -- grounding refs ride the envelope refs[]; factual requires validated grounding (VALIDATE-FACTUAL-ASSERT, sec 6.1); default register is narrative

xrefs.$comment: cross-boundary URIs; medium:// admissible iff the referenced type is in the wire registry's NON-MINTABLE (warrant-class) set -- wire.md sec 3 names it (the HOME; this contract cites it and never hard-codes it: the mint-restricted types that CERTIFY a boundary crossing); act://corr ok; https:// rejected unless resolvable to the act that fetched it (sec 6.1 rule 4)

memory.supersede.$comment: memory family (sec 3/6) -- assert body + target_memory_id; atomic replace; old version stays queryable as-of the past

memory.pin.$comment: memory family (sec 3/6) -- consolidation-immune + S0-eligible; over pin_budget => E_PIN_BUDGET

memory.forget.$comment: memory family (sec 3/6) -- render tombstone; the ledger retains (true erasure: identity-firewall.md)

memory.recall.$comment: memory family (sec 3/6) -- journaled READ; no fold consumes it. Minted only by the MODEL-INITIATED verb: assembly-time RECALL_ASSEMBLY (sec 7.3) is UNJOURNALED -- the frame manifest's segments[S4].items IS its durable record

frame.$comment: structure family -- the frame manifest (sec 7.2 step 9 / 7.5); written by the assembler at standard durability; the audit query ('why did the cell not know X at tick t') reads segments[].items vs dropped

ledger_head.$comment: h -- the ledger head seq candidates were gathered at

dropped.$comment: each drop {ref, tok, salience, reason} (sec 7.2 step 5)

fork.child.$comment: structure family (sec 3/10) -- gold; the parent side of a fork (child side = its genesis.forked_from); lineage lives in BOTH ledgers

consolidation.$comment: structure family (sec 3/11) -- gold on install; a failing digest NEVER installs; installs happen only at task boundaries (the cache seam)

digest_artifact.$comment: REEL 5-field digest artifact ref, pre-chunked <= 512 tok

cold_eyes.$comment: L2 rotates per pass over the available !=L1 set (sec 11 step 4)
